prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System (dry fuels, steep terrain, WUI). Baseline: segmentation, time sync, health checks, audit logs; coordination records retain timestamps, participant identities, radio path status. Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): primary interface, mapping workspace; opens triage case above threshold; records triage reasons; holds jurisdictional constraints before Drone Pilot Operator briefing; marks failed radio route impaired (Orion acknowledges); shows crew acknowledgements beside aviation tasks. North Lookout Camera Mast: time-stamped smoke bearing with PTZ/confidence; sends Thermal Spot Snippet. South Lookout Camera Mast: separate bearing track for triangulation/uncertainty ellipse; produces Camera Cleaning Log. Both: hardened power, licensed backhaul (cellular fallback). Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): launch/recovery/charging; produces Battery Swap Ticket (used by Drone Pilot Operator for endurance). Drone Tasking Service: packages objectives as footprints, altitude bands, revisit intervals; no flight-release authority; no launch conflicting with active Marigold aviation lane. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern): advisories, perimeter; detects heat, smoke edges, flame fronts, spot fires in orthorectified registered imagery; may down-weight Smoke Classifier Module when quality degraded; score is not fire declaration. Smoke Classifier Module: Ridge Shadow Mask; smoke likelihood, growth trend, obscuration flag. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle): Wind Shift Bulletin. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger): recorded voice, bridges paths, preserves speaker identity. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold): aviation lanes. East Retardant Loading Pump: Retardant Batch Slip; West Retardant Loading Pump. Crewline Mobile Tablet: Helitack Crew Leader acknowledges air-to-ground instructions, reports crews in drop/recon areas; receives only released confirmed context. Actors: County Emergency Liaison sends Drone Corridor Permit. Duty Detection Officer (Orion): reviews triage, uses snippet to accept observations into assessment queue, recommends escalation. Drone Pilot Operator. Air Attack Supervisor (Redtail): deconflicts routes, verifies ground clear before authorizing flight, checks restrictions vs Lantern perimeter. Tanker Base Manager: confirms pump readiness before assignment. States: Confirmed Ignition (persistent cue plus corroboration) enables suppression planning; if airspace delayed, planning visible, dispatch blocked. Airspace Restricted set by Portal; tasking conditional until Redtail confirms. No autonomous

New part:
S112: Analytic results are not displayed as final fireline until confidence thresholds, sensor age, and positional error are applied as explicit map attributes.
S113: The MesoWest Weather Fusion Node ingests station observations, forecast grids, and local quality checks to maintain the wind, humidity, temperature, and stability fields used by the spread model.
S114: Brindle publishes a time-indexed weather update that marks significant forecast changes and identifies which map products require recomputation.
S115: Weather fields are interpolated across the incident area with terrain-aware weighting so ridge, drainage, and slope effects are represented at operational map scale.
S116: Geospatial overlays include fuels, slope, aspect, roads, structures, water sources, jurisdiction boundaries, evacuation zones, and known communications coverage.
S117: The fire behavior model combines the accepted perimeter, recent growth vectors, weather fields, and fuel conditions to estimate short-term spread direction and rate.
S118: Model output is expressed as probability bands rather than a single line so supervisors can see both the most likely path and the practical planning margin.
S119: Emberhall renders the current perimeter, projected spread, resource positions, and decision annotations into a common operating picture with role-based symbology.
S120: The Caldera Incident Command Portal produces the Crew Staging Pin from the approved map layer and assigns it an effective time, location accuracy, and incident identifier.
S121: Operational recommendations are generated from rule checks that compare projected fire arrival times with values at risk, road access, crew travel time, and aircraft availability.
S122: Recommendations may include confirming an ignition, increasing camera monitoring, requesting drone coverage, preparing aviation options, repositioning ground crews, or notifying county partners.
S123: The Air Attack Supervisor receives map products that emphasize projected columns, flight hazards, target areas, and timing constraints without obscuring ground resource information.
S124: The County Emergency Liaison receives a simplified view that preserves perimeter confidence, threatened areas, and recommended public safety coordination actions while hiding tactical details not needed for civil coordination.
S125: Every map product records source time, processing time, model version, analyst acceptance, and supersession status so users can distinguish current guidance from archived assessments.
S126: When inputs conflict, the common operating picture shows the conflict explicitly and requires review before the affected recommendation is promoted for command use.
S127: Suppression planning begins after the Caldera Incident Command Portal promotes an accepted fire location into the operational map and marks it available for aviation review.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
